races.name: Summer Saturday Series At Doncaster Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Pure Panel Management Handicap (Rnd)

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter in this field and likely to have things entirely its own way up front; recent form shows a win over this trip on good ground 12 days ago, Alex Jary claiming 3lb is useful, but the [STYLE_FIT] tag flags it is slightly racing outside its optimal prominent role rather than pure lead.|

runners_data.name: Straight A
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with multiple placed efforts at 8f on good ground for Michael Appleby, though 37 days off the track and a 0-from-15 record on similar going is a concern; maps naturally just off the pace but needs to improve on a modest strike rate.|

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: Holds-up but carries a clear finishing concern — flagged as fading in the finish — and recent form of 990000 makes this Andrew Mullen-ridden runner very hard to trust despite the Ben Haslam yard showing 2 wins from 14 runners in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for the in-form David O'Meara yard (8 wins from 55 in 14 days) and the horse has strong placed form at 7f on good ground, but its natural hold-up style means it needs a strong pace to close into, and a controlled tempo here is against it.|

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: David Probert partners this hold-up operator who has placed form at 8f but needs things to go right from the rear; the race shape doesn't naturally set this up, though good-to-firm ground is fine and 29 days since last run is not a concern.|

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Multiple winner in recent form (1-1521) with a win at 8f on soft and a placed effort at 8f on good, this Fahey-trained four-year-old in a tongue tie naturally wants to race prominently and this race shape suits that role well; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is an added bonus.|

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good going 13 days ago with Oisin Orr aboard, and wears a tongue strap; Sam England's yard is 5-from-16 in the past fortnight and this prominent racer is very well placed tactically to travel close to Amidst The Chaos and produce a forward challenge.|

runners_data.name: Tilani
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at 8f for Ian Williams suggest genuine form, but this is a true prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield because the field is over-supplied with forward types — Edward Greatrex will find it harder than usual to position this horse where it wants to race, tempering its chance.|

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is busy (8-from-106 in 14 days) and this horse has solid placed form on good ground, but it is a genuine hold-up runner that has been pushed into a midfield mapping due to congestion at the rear — it will not be racing in its natural sweet spot, which is a real disadvantage in what sets up as a truly-run prominent race.|

races.paceDynamic: Amidst The Chaos is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to push hard for the lead, this 1m round course at Doncaster should be run at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured burn. Straight A, Mwafaq, and Yafaarr are all prominent-style horses who will want to track close to the pace but are unlikely to seriously dispute it, leaving Amidst The Chaos to dictate terms and set a tempo entirely of its own choosing on good-to-firm ground. The field is notably top-heavy with prominent types — Tilani and Valentine Catcher have been redistributed from their natural positions because this shape simply cannot accommodate so many forward-hunting runners, meaning those two will likely find themselves racing out of role. A controlled front-running tempo on a flat, fair track favours horses that can travel prominently in behind and produce a clean, sustained finish — the profile that benefits most clearly here is the prominent-to-midfield racer who gets a trouble-free trip and can quicken into the straight without burning matches early.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Track
scenarios.trigger: If Amidst The Chaos dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the race is decided by those travelling prominently in behind.
scenarios.body: If Amidst The Chaos dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the race is decided by those travelling prominently in behind.

scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely slow early and the race turns into a sprint finish, compressing the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Amidst The Chaos exploits an uncontested lead and converts from the front under Alex Jary's positive ride.
scenarios.body: If Amidst The Chaos exploits an uncontested lead and converts from the front under Alex Jary's positive ride.

scenarios.label: D

watchPoints.text: Mwafaq and Yafaarr are both naturally prominent and both in strong recent form — watch which of the two secures the cleaner position tracking Amidst The Chaos, as that horse will have a significant tactical advantage in the straight.

Amidst The Chaos sets its own pace but its [STYLE_FIT] tag means it is marginally out of its optimal pattern; if Straight A or Mwafaq push harder than expected in the first two furlongs, the front-runner's advantage could erode quickly.

Tilani's two recent wins make it a form danger but Edward Greatrex will likely find this horse boxed in among a congested midfield — monitor the draw and early positioning at the start to see whether it can recover any prominent ground.

Al Muqdad brings Daniel Tudhope and the in-form O'Meara yard but is entirely dependent on a strong pace developing; if the gallop remains controlled, its hold-up style leaves it with too much ground to make up in the Doncaster straight.
Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for this race despite the header listing "Good" — all runners have acceptable going profiles, so no runner is significantly disadvantaged on surface grounds alone.

races.name: Believe Money Group Handicap

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has shown course and distance form on Good ground and arrives just 12 days since his last run, making him fresh and fit; Liam Wright (5) takes 5lb off, which is a meaningful allowance in this grade, and his two placed efforts at this trip on similar ground make him one of the more interesting hold-up types if he can secure a clear run.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old has winning form at 5f on Good ground and solid recent placing, but his natural instinct is to race from the rear, and with so many other hold-up types in this field he is unlikely to find daylight as cleanly as he would in a smaller, faster-pace field — the redistribution to a midfield map position reflects a congested back end rather than any change in his tactical tendency.

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old sprinter for Antony Brittain who carries no wins or places from 15 runs on Good going in his recent history, and his form string of 0024-0 raises serious questions about consistency at the top of his cycle; he is a rear-of-field runner by nature, and having been placed on Tapeta rather than turf recently, this Good to Firm turf contest looks demanding for him at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby fields this four-year-old whose last six runs have all come at 6f, making the drop to 5f today an untested variable — his finishing efforts at six suggest he stays well but may lack the early zip that a true 5f specialist needs on fast ground; Duran Fentiman takes the ride, and while Easterby fires a high volume of runners, his 14-day record of 7 from 98 is modest, tempering enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old has managed just one third from eight starts on Good or faster ground and arrives with no wins at any trip on turf recently, which is a concern on today's Good to Firm conditions; Lauren Young claims 5lb and holds amateur racing experience, though the horse's natural running style — well held up and finishing late — is the most crowded profile in this race.

runners_data.name: Paddy's Day
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the key pace influence in this race — Nigel Tinkler saddles him just seven days after his last outing, indicating he is in a good place physically, and he has placed twice from five starts at 5f, showing tactical speed over this trip; tongue tie is applied, and the question is simply whether he can sustain his lead long enough on Going to Firm ground once the closers switch on behind him.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old has two second-place finishes from five starts at 5f on Good ground and arrives quickly (8 days since last run), suggesting he is in form and ready to go again; Edward Greatrex takes the ride, and with a strong profile of placing on this exact trip and going combination, Dyonisos is well-placed among the hold-up brigade to secure a handy tracking position and challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Paddy's Day is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, he should dictate from the gates at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. The remainder of the field — Moulin Booj, Emerald Harmony, Mondammej, Miraculous, Oriental Prince and Dyonisos — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, meaning the pace is thin and Paddy's Day controls the tempo entirely. With just one horse setting the fractions, a comfortable, measured pace is the likeliest outcome, which historically at this flat, straight course favours those who can travel prominently or make a smooth, well-timed run from just off the leader. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can secure a tracking position close to Paddy's Day — those are the profiles to side with — but it is worth noting that this field contains far more true hold-up types than the pace map can place; Emerald Harmony, Mondammej, Miraculous, Oriental Prince and Dyonisos are all genuine rear-of-field horses redistributed toward midfield on the map, and it is Dyonisos and Moulin Booj — the most active hold-up horses with the best course and going profiles — who are likeliest to secure the most advantageous tracking positions.

watchPoints.text: Dyonisos has placed twice at 5f on Good ground and arrives on a short turnaround in apparent form — watch whether Greatrex can position him closest to Paddy's Day to exploit the anticipated pace gap in the final furlong.

Paddy's Day's front-running dominance is the race's central tactical fact — if he quickens away from the gates cleanly and no one goes with him, the entire field is chasing him from 3f out on Good to Firm ground.

Moulin Booj receives a 5lb apprentice claim from Liam Wright, which significantly reduces his weight burden in a tight handicap — watch for him being produced widest of all to find daylight in the closing stages.

With five genuine hold-up horses compressed into the back half, traffic problems inside the final 2f are a real risk — any horse caught with nowhere to go approaching the final furlong should be noted for future reference.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for the 3:10 (not Good as listed in the race header) — this slightly faster surface will suit those with clean early pace and may stretch stamina reserves for the older horses like Mondammej and Oriental Prince who rarely show on turf in these conditions.

races.name: Instarmac Group Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Military Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for David O'Meara whose similar-going record reads 2 runs, 0 wins, 0 places — the step back to 1m2f after a 12f run suits the distance concern less than it might appear; headgear noted, 22 days fresh, needs a clean passage off a sound pace.|

runners_data.name: Redbud Sixteen
runners_data.note: The one genuine front-runner here; two consecutive wins over 10-11f on good ground for Charlie Pike give real confidence, and with Edward Greatrex aboard and no pace rival to hassle him, he can dictate exactly the tempo he wants.|

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's consistent prominent racer has a strong similar-going profile over shorter trips but is stepping up in distance; Pat Dobbs takes over and will likely push for one of the contested early prominent spots — form figures show a place last time at 8f on good.|

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Dour hold-up type for David O'Meara whose entire recent hist is run at 10-12f on good ground, giving genuine course-and-distance profile; OR 87 is the joint-highest in the field and Tudhope's handling of traffic will be crucial off this pace shape.|

runners_data.name: Footwork
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's confirmed prominent racer has won twice over 9f on good ground recently; the 34-day break is the only flag, but the OR 87 and Connor Beasley's clean positional riding make this a credible player if it gets to its natural front-rank berth.|

runners_data.name: Serenity Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile that has shown placed form at 12f on good ground but recent form reads three zeros; James Horton's yard is winless in the last 14 days, and the horse's best chance depends on a messy race creating gaps.|

runners_data.name: Be Patient
runners_data.note: Three-year-old making its first run in 239 days for Edward Bethell with limited form — just two runs, both on standard — and a prominent style that will need to compete for a congested berth; the layoff is a significant unknown at this level.|

runners_data.name: Bintknight
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's lightly-raced three-year-old has won over 10f on good ground and carries genuine hold-up tendencies, but with more hold-up types than map positions allow, it is placed in midfield rather than naturally drifting to the rear; discount its chance slightly in a race where it cannot reproduce its natural stalking role.|

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; had prominent form at 10f on good and soft ground for Simon & Ed Crisford, but the absence means it has no bearing on the race shape or outcome.|

races.paceDynamic: Redbud Sixteen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one rival willing to lead, should secure a clean, uncontested passage from the gates and dictate a sustainable gallop over this flat 1m2f at Doncaster on good-to-firm ground. Four runners — Eupator, Footwork, Be Patient, and to a lesser extent Bintknight — want the prominent position just behind, creating a likely scramble for the first two or three berths in the early furlongs that could generate minor interference and congestion approaching the two-furlong marker. This field contains more prominent-minded types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate: of those competing for the prominent slots, Footwork and Eupator look most capable of actually securing them given their pace profiles and jockey quality, while Bintknight — a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — is unlikely to replicate its natural position. With the pace honest but not injuriously fast, and Redbud Sixteen able to control the tempo, this race shape most favours confirmed hold-up horses who settle comfortably, travel wide of any midfield traffic, and produce a sustained late run — Prince Of The Seas and Military Air have the profiles, but the outcome also hinges on whether the congestion at 2-3 out releases them cleanly.

scenarios.title: Redbud Sixteen Controls, Closers Finish

scenarios.body: If Redbud Sixteen dictates a fair but not killing tempo, the race sets up for one clean late burst from the hold-up runners.

scenarios.body: If the early scramble for position drains the hold-up horses' energy and the pace is stronger than it looks, prominent types hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redbud Sixteen Front-to-Finish

scenarios.body: If the tempo drops to a crawl and no rival applies sustained pressure, Redbud Sixteen steals it from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes a significant incident 2-3 out, a horse wide of the trouble collects.
scenarios.body: If the prominent congestion causes a significant incident 2-3 out, a horse wide of the trouble collects.

watchPoints.text: Eupator, Footwork, and Be Patient are all competing for the same two prominent berths — watch for barging and position-grabbing in the first two furlongs that could check any of the three and shuffle the race order entirely.

Prince Of The Seas and Military Air must find unimpeded runs off the home bend; if the prominent congestion backs up into midfield at the 2-3 furlong marker, both O'Meara runners risk being boxed at the critical moment.

Redbud Sixteen's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the fulcrum of the whole race — if Footwork's rider decides to press and test the leader before the straight, the race shape shifts materially and the lead scenario probability collapses.

Be Patient has been off for 239 days and tackles a contested prominent position in a 9-runner field on debut after a long break — fitness and sharpness are genuine unknowns that could see it drop out quickly and cause interference behind.

Bintknight's natural running style is hold-up but it is mapped and likely to race in midfield; track how it settles in the first half-mile — if it gets shuffled wider than expected, it could find clear running ahead of the true closers.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap

runners_data.name: Ishe Worth Agamble
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has shown ability at this course and trip on good ground (placed twice at 6f/Good) but wears a tp headgear first-time combination and, as a genuine hold-up horse, will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal in this shape — that compromise weakens his chance of hitting the line at full throttle.|

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's four-year-old returns after a 35-day break having run creditably at this course before, but naturally operates from the very back of the field; in a race with minimal pace pressure, arriving from the rear on good-to-firm ground will require a clear passage that the congested midfield may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Cosmic Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old has posted back-to-back placed efforts at 6f on good and standard ground and ran well here 19 days ago, suggesting course fitness is strong; a visor is worn and, as a genuine hold-up type, the relatively slow pace of this race is a mild concern, though the ability to sit mid-division should help.|

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for David O'Meara on this three-year-old who was placed at 6f on good ground just seven days ago, suggesting freshness is not an issue; visor-wearing and a natural hold-up horse, Tudhope's positional intelligence could see her positioned advantageously just off the midfield shuffle rather than deep in the pack.|

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's three-year-old has an unknown style profile and hasn't run for 60 days, which is a notable concern; the sole run on good-to-firm-adjacent ground showed no form (9th), and with limited recent evidence on this configuration, the price must account for considerable uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Tony Culhane and Stella Barclay's three-year-old has been gelded during the campaign and the trainer has drawn a blank in 5 runners over 14 days; his best result came at 7f on good, and dropping back to 6f on this faster surface while racing out of his natural deep-closing position makes a winning performance very hard to construct.|

runners_data.name: Maxi Boy
runners_data.note: Fionn McSharry's nine-year-old carries top weight of 142lbs and is a consistent hold-up performer, though recent form shows two eighth-place finishes; at this age and weight level, the good-to-firm ground and uncontested pace are unlikely to provide the strong gallop he typically needs to get competitive late.|

runners_data.name: Carlton And Co
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, Michael and David Easterby's seven-year-old won over this C&D in a similar scenario and wears a first-time visor; Joanna Mason has a positive record with her and with no rivals to push the tempo, a STYLE_FIT tag reflects the risk she is asked to make all — that is exactly what her form says she can do.|

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old has recorded zero wins from 15 starts on similar good-to-firm-adjacent ground, and while he wears a p headgear (possibly cheekpieces), his natural rear-of-field style is squeezed into a midfield position in this shape — a combination of out-of-role racing and a blank win record on this going makes him one of the more difficult cases to support.|

races.paceDynamic: Carlton And Co is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press from the gates, she should coast into a comfortable lead down the Doncaster straight and dictate every fraction on good-to-firm ground. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up horses — Kings Merchant, Ishe Worth Agamble, Get Up Everybody and Go Victor are all natural rear-of-field types who have been mapped to midfield simply because the race shape cannot accommodate them all at the back — meaning the true rear positions will be congested and those horses will race closer than preferred. With Carlton And Co controlling a sustainable, uncontested gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a prominent or mid-division berth and produce a clean run through the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who will be shuffled wide or find traffic from an unusually crowded rear group. Cosmic Clarets and Come On Over, carrying genuine hold-up profiles but with the ability to travel handy on this configuration, are best placed; deep closers dependent on a true strong pace to run into are at a structural disadvantage here.

watchPoints.text: Carlton And Co — if she breaks cleanly and is allowed to go unchallenged in front, the entire race shape hinges on whether the hold-up field can close quickly enough on good-to-firm; she is the single most influential horse in this race.

Ishe Worth Agamble and Get Up Everybody — both natural deep closers forced into midfield positions, watch for either being checked or short of room in a bunched final furlong if the pace does not quicken sufficiently to spread the field.

Come On Over — runs just seven days after her last start; watch for signs in the early stages that the quick turnaround has left her flat, particularly given Daniel Tudhope may need to work harder to secure position in an out-of-shape rear group.

Maxi Boy — top weight of 142lbs is significant on good-to-firm ground over 6f for a nine-year-old; if he fails to travel with his usual fluency in the first half of the race, he is unlikely to recover on this surface.

Medyg — 60 days off, unknown style, and trainer striking at just 1 from 6 in 14 days; watch how she loads and whether she travels early, as those signals will clarify whether she is a live outsider or one to oppose with confidence.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Chicory
runners_data.note: Produced a good win over 6f on Good going recently (OR 79) and handles this surface well, but is a natural hold-up filly stepping down to 5f for the first time in this campaign, which shortens the track she has to make up ground.|

runners_data.name: Saffron Dandy
runners_data.note: Won on Soft last time and holds a recent victory on her form string, but her sim-going record on Good or Firm ground reads 0 wins from 4 relevant runs, which is a meaningful flag on today's Good To Firm surface at Doncaster.|

runners_data.name: Cressida Wildes
runners_data.note: Holds a visor in her headgear record and won off a similar mark at Sandown last term; a genuine hold-up filly by trade whose natural position is at the rear, though the surplus of closers in this field means she is likely to find herself in midfield by default rather than design.|

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Running off a quick 7-day turnaround for Scott Dixon, whose T14 strike rate is modest at 1/19; her form shows consistent placing at this trip on similar going, but she finishes races rather than makes them and will need a gap to open in the final furlong that may not materialise.|

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: The only genuinely prominent-going runner aside from Eternal Sunshine, giving Harry Davies a live tactical position just off the leader; won at 6f on Good going and has placed multiple times at similar marks, making him the most natural beneficiary if Eternal Sunshine weakens.|

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Two wins at 5f on Good ground this season and an excellent sim-going profile (2W4P from 6 relevant runs) make her form credentials strong; by nature a hold-up filly who will be further forward than ideal given the field composition, but her 5f course-trip profile is the most compelling among the closers.|

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner and pace-setter for this race; however, her recent form shows three consecutive mid-to-back finishes on Good or Good To Firm ground (positions 9, 10, 13), and although she sets the shape, whether she can sustain the advantage to the line is a real question.|

runners_data.name: Alpine Girl
runners_data.note: Two wins at 5f on Good going and a strong sim-going record of 5W7P underline her ability on fast ground; a natural hold-up or rear-of-field filly who has been off 47 days, and with the trainer Julie Camacho yet to strike in the T14 window (0/17), the fitness question is live.|

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Sunshine is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Good To Firm sprint at Doncaster and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her for the lead, she should bowl along uncontested from the gates and set a sustainable rather than scorching tempo. Space Bear is the only other prominently-drawn, forward-going type and will likely slot in just behind, giving the pace shape a clear single-file leader with a compact chasing group. The remainder of the field — Chicory, Saffron Dandy, Cressida Wildes, Alondra, Dragon Spin and Alpine Girl — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field horses, meaning the closing sector will be crowded with horses seeking the same late ground and many unable to achieve their true tactical position. This race shape, with a lone uncontested leader on fast ground over the minimum trip, strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a horse that can control the tempo and quicken clear before the closers, hampered by their own congestion, can get organised. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate; of those competing for prominent slots, Eternal Sunshine is best placed to lead, with Space Bear most likely to actually secure the second position closest to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Sunshine's recent form reads 13th, 13th, 10th, 9th on Good to Firm-type ground — watch whether she actually leads with purpose or fades markedly once headed, which would flip the entire race shape.
Dragon Spin has two wins and four places from six runs at 5f on Good going — if she can find a clear passage from midfield in the final furlong she is the most dangerous closer in the race.

Space Bear is the only other forward-going type and if he presses Eternal Sunshine hard from the gate rather than tracking comfortably, the pace could be stronger than expected, significantly improving the closers' chances.

Alpine Girl is 47 days since last run and trainer Julie Camacho has no winners from 17 runners in the T14 window — monitor market moves in the final hour for any indication of stable confidence before committing to her.

The field contains four redistributed hold-up horses (Cressida Wildes, Alondra, Dragon Spin, Alpine Girl) all competing for the same late ground — watch for traffic congestion and lack of clear runs in the final 100 yards, which could result in unlucky-in-running horses that merit reassessment next time.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Bami
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who led and won over 7f on Good at Goodwood ten days ago; uncontested pace-setter here gives her every chance of controlling fractions, though a good draw and stable form (Tom Dascombe 1 from 12 last 14 days) make her a danger to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Why Because
runners_data.note: Holds-up off the pace over 6f-8f for Paul Midgley (1 from 24 last 14 days), returns from a 43-day break and has been running consistently at similar distances on Good, though the trip up to 7f and the moderate pace she'll face from the rear look against her.|

runners_data.name: Borjina
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 7f on Good ground at Goodwood last time for Edward Bethell (busy yard, 3 from 31 last 14 days); entirely at home in this shape — tracks the leader and has proven she can quicken off a sound pace at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Seeing Stars
runners_data.note: Contested the pace in each recent start at 7f, hitting the frame four times from five attempts at the distance, and Harry Davies rides a horse whose style is perfectly suited to shadowing Bami; the lack of a win from those consistent efforts is a mild concern.|

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a filly who has finished in the rear half of the field in all four runs on Soft/Standard, with her sole Good-ground run a distant sixth over 7f; stepping back from a route and facing a controlled pace from a hold-up position is awkward.|

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K R Burke's filly returns from a 68-day absence and holds her form at 7f-8f on Good ground, with three consecutive placed runs in similar conditions; holds-up naturally and will need a strongly-run race to arrive late — the controlled pace is a risk.|

runners_data.name: Accademia
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly finished fifth on Good over 8f last time and is a genuine hold-up horse who will race further forward than she would like here due to the abundance of closers in the field; Kieran Shoemark can make the best of it but the position is not ideal.|

runners_data.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners_data.note: Won twice in the last month on Good ground, including over 7f, and Joanna Mason has partnered the horse for both recent victories; the most potent hold-up threat because her recent form is verifiably strong and the distance and going are confirmed suits.|

runners_data.name: South Coast Star
runners_data.note: David Probert's mount bounced back to win over 7f at Sandown last time and is effective racing prominently, though Good ground form is thin (one run, seventh of 11); Hugo Palmer's yard is in fair form and she could benefit from tracking Bami closely.|

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: A true deep hold-up horse who has been placed only once in five runs and has struggled repeatedly on Good ground; mapped closer to midfield than she would naturally run, and form figures of 74-364 do not inspire confidence in this competitive shape.|

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good for Tim Easterby (high-volume yard) and has shown reasonable consistency at the trip, with headgear worn previously; races from hold-up, which the pace map has pushed her into midfield from — the 7f on Good to Firm is not a confirmed strong suit.|

runners_data.name: Uncertainty
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's filly has returned form figures of 4-8797, all on Good or better ground, and has never threatened to win; runs from hold-up but is positioned in midfield on this map due to the field's make-up, and her recent form makes her difficult to support.|

races.paceDynamic: Bami is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead from this 12-runner field, she should bowl along uncontested on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster's straight seven, dictating a rhythm that suits her own stamina reserves. The pace is unlikely to be suicidal — a lone leader rarely fires up a genuine scorcher — meaning the fractions will be controlled and the premium will fall on those able to track closely and sustain their effort into the final two furlongs rather than those making up late ground from well off the pace. Borjina, Seeing Stars and South Coast Star are the natural prominent challengers who can sit just behind Bami and pounce, while the large hold-up contingent — Gunalt Wavelength, Light The Night Up, Why Because, Sailor's Return — face a stiffer task finishing from off a sustainable pace on a flat, galloping track. This race shape emphatically favours prominent racers who can shadow the leader and challenge from two out; closers face a stiff task as the even pace will not generate a strong late surge. The field holds more true hold-up horses than can all fill rear positions — Accademia, Uncertainty, Vega's Virtue and Angel Summer are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because they are unlikely to get their natural spot, with Bami and the prominent trio (Borjina, Seeing Stars, South Coast Star) most likely to control the race from the front.

watchPoints.text: Gunalt Wavelength has won twice on Good ground in the past month at 6f-7f for Joanna Mason — if she gets a clear run from midfield in the final quarter-mile, she is the most credible late challenger to the prominent horses.

Bami must be monitored at the start — if anything disturbs her habitual front-running and she drops away from the early lead, the race shape collapses and prominent runners like Borjina lose their reference point.

Borjina and Seeing Stars are both naturally prominent, and if they press Bami too hard too soon the pace could rise sharply and paradoxically bring the stronger hold-up finishers like Gunalt Wavelength into play; watch the early fractions.

The Good to Firm official going (confirmed by the day's going reports across all distances) means the track is riding fast — any horse who has only shown form on Soft or Standard surfaces should be discounted, narrowing the credible field materially.

Light The Night Up has been off for 68 days — monitor market moves in the final hour, as K R Burke's yard is capable of producing fit horses first time back, and a market move would suggest confidence.
